use_cases.label: Get a patient's records for treatment

routes.title: Your EHR vendor's network or a national framework
routes.summary: Your EHR looks up a patient at other organizations and pulls their documents through a network or framework your vendor has joined.
routes.who_can_use: Clinicians and organizations whose EHR or health IT vendor connects to the network or framework.
routes.rule: The participation agreement and policies of the network or framework your vendor joined.
routes.standard: IHE cross-community document query and retrieve (XCA); some networks also accept HL7 FHIR queries.
routes.how_to_join: Ask your EHR vendor which networks or frameworks it connects to and how your organization turns on access.

routes.title: Your state or regional HIE
routes.summary: Your organization joins a health information exchange and queries it for a patient's records held by other members.
routes.who_can_use: Providers and other organizations that sign the HIE's participation agreement.
routes.rule: The HIE's participation agreement and the health information laws of the state it operates in.
routes.standard: Query-based exchange; the standard varies by HIE and is stated on its entry.
routes.how_to_join: Contact the HIE listed for your state on this page.

sources.title: What is HIE?, Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy / ONC

routes.title: TEFCA, through a QHIN
routes.summary: Your organization connects to TEFCA through a QHIN, directly or through a participant of one, and queries other TEFCA participants for a patient's records.
routes.who_can_use: Organizations that sign on as a Participant or Subparticipant of a designated QHIN.
routes.rule: TEFCA Common Agreement, Treatment exchange purpose, with the Treatment exchange purpose implementation SOP.
routes.standard: IHE document exchange of C-CDA documents, as set by the QHIN Technical Framework; the RCE's FHIR roadmap adds HL7 FHIR as an option alongside the required IHE transactions.
routes.how_to_join: Choose a designated QHIN, or an HIE or vendor that participates in one, and sign its participation agreement.

routes.title: A Direct message
routes.summary: A clinician sends records to a known recipient's Direct address, an encrypted message pushed to one address rather than a search across organizations.
routes.who_can_use: Anyone holding a Direct address issued by a health information service provider (HISP), which is often supplied through the EHR.
routes.rule: The trust framework and certificate trust bundles of the sender's and receiver's HISPs.
routes.standard: Direct secure messaging (Applicability Statement for Secure Health Transport, Version 1.2).
routes.how_to_join: Get a Direct address from a HISP; ask your EHR vendor first, since EHR certification includes Direct messaging.

routes.title: Your provider's patient API, through an app you choose
routes.summary: You connect an app to your provider's certified FHIR API and download your own records into it.
routes.who_can_use: Patients, and the apps they authorize, at providers whose health IT is certified to 45 CFR 170.315(g)(10).
routes.rule: ONC Health IT Certification Program: 45 CFR 170.315(g)(10) and the API Condition of Certification, 45 CFR 170.404.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 with the US Core implementation guide, with SMART authorization.
routes.how_to_join: Pick an app that connects to your provider's FHIR API and sign in with your patient portal account when the app asks.

routes.title: Your health plan's Patient Access API
routes.summary: You connect an app to your health plan's API to get your claims and encounter data, including cost, and a defined set of clinical data.
routes.who_can_use: Members of Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid and CHIP programs and managed care plans, and Qualified Health Plan issuers on the federally facilitated exchanges.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Patient Access final rule (CMS-9115-F); CMS-0057-F adds prior authorization information.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 (Release 4.0.1) API.
routes.how_to_join: Pick an app that connects to your plan's Patient Access API, or ask your plan which apps it supports.

routes.who_can_use: Individuals, through an Individual Access Services provider connected to TEFCA by a QHIN, Participant or Subparticipant.

routes.standard: Set by the QHIN Technical Framework and the Individual Access Services SOP.

routes.summary: CMS publishes practitioners, organizations, locations and endpoints as public FHIR files and a search site.
routes.who_can_use: Anyone; the directory is public.
routes.rule: Public data release by CMS; no participation agreement.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 resources in bulk NDJSON files, listed in a download manifest.
routes.how_to_join: Search at directory.cms.gov or download the bulk files listed in its manifest.

routes.title: EHR vendors' published endpoint lists
routes.summary: Developers of certified patient APIs publish the FHIR service base URLs of their customers, with each organization's name, location and identifier.
routes.who_can_use: Anyone; the lists must be published at no charge.
routes.rule: API Condition of Certification, 45 CFR 170.404(b)(2), service base URL publication.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 Endpoint and Organization resources collected in a Bundle, reviewed quarterly.
routes.how_to_join: Find the list in the EHR developer's published API documentation.

routes.summary: Health plans publish their provider directory through a public API that apps and other providers can read.
routes.who_can_use: Anyone; the rule requires the directory to be publicly available.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Patient Access final rule (CMS-9115-F); applies to Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and CHIP, not to Qualified Health Plan issuers on the federally facilitated exchanges.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 API.
routes.how_to_join: Find the API in the health plan's developer documentation.

routes.title: Direct address directories
routes.summary: HISPs publish their users' Direct addresses to directories, and providers can record a Direct address or FHIR endpoint in NPPES as digital contact information.
routes.who_can_use: HISPs that contribute to an aggregated directory get access to it; NPPES contact information is entered by each provider.
routes.rule: The directory policies of the HISPs' trust framework; the CMS-9115-F digital contact information policy for NPPES.
routes.standard: Direct addresses; aggregated directory built to support FHIR API access.
routes.how_to_join: Ask your HISP whether it contributes to and reads an aggregated directory, and keep your NPPES digital contact information current.

routes.summary: A plan member's app pulls their claims, encounter and clinical data from the plan; CMS-0057-F adds prior authorization information (excluding drugs) by January 1, 2027.
routes.who_can_use: Members of impacted payers and the apps they authorize.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Patient Access final rule (CMS-9115-F), as amended by the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F).
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR R4 API.
routes.how_to_join: Members connect an app; app developers register with each payer's API.

routes.title: Provider Access API
routes.summary: An in-network provider pulls claims, encounter, USCDI and prior authorization data for patients it treats, unless the patient opts out; payers must implement it by January 1, 2027.
routes.who_can_use: In-network providers with a treatment relationship to the patient, as set by the payer's attribution process.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F). CMS states the exact compliance dates vary by type of payer.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR API.
routes.how_to_join: Ask each impacted payer how it attributes patients to your organization and how to connect to its Provider Access API.

routes.title: Payer-to-Payer API
routes.summary: When a patient who opted in changes plans, the new payer requests the patient's claims, encounter, USCDI and prior authorization data from the old one. The old payer must share data with a date of service within five years of the request. Payers must implement it by January 1, 2027.
routes.who_can_use: Impacted payers, for patients who opt in.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F). CMS states the exact compliance dates vary by type of payer.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR API.
routes.how_to_join: Applies to impacted payers; each builds and maintains its own API.

routes.title: Prior Authorization API
routes.summary: A provider's system finds whether an item or service needs prior authorization, what documentation is required, and sends the request and gets the decision; required beginning January 1, 2027.
routes.who_can_use: Providers requesting prior authorization from an impacted payer, for items and services other than drugs.
routes.rule: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F), with HHS enforcement discretion for the HIPAA X12 278 standard when an all-FHIR API is used.
routes.standard: HL7 FHIR API; X12 278 may also be offered.
routes.how_to_join: Ask your EHR vendor and each impacted payer how to connect to the payer's Prior Authorization API.

routes.title: Event notifications through an HIE
routes.summary: A hospital sends admit, discharge and transfer messages to an HIE, which passes notices on to the patient's other providers.
routes.who_can_use: Hospitals that send to the HIE, and providers that receive its notices under its participation agreement.
routes.rule: Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.24(d), which lets a hospital send notifications through an intermediary; the HIE's participation agreement.
routes.standard: HL7 v2 ADT messages (HL7 2.5.1, the content standard named in 45 CFR 170.205(d)(2)).
routes.how_to_join: Contact the HIE listed for your state on this page.

routes.title: Hospital e-notifications under the Medicare Conditions of Participation

routes.who_can_use: Post-acute care providers and the practitioners or groups the rule names as recipients.
routes.rule: Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.24(d), added by CMS-9115-F; applies to hospitals whose systems conform to the content standard at 45 CFR 170.205(d)(2).
routes.standard: HL7 v2 ADT messages (HL7 2.5.1).
routes.how_to_join: Ask the hospital, or its HIE, how it sends notifications and how to be listed as a recipient.

glossary.definition: Health information exchange: an organization or network that moves patient health data between providers and other authorized parties.
Qualified Health Information Network: an organization designated under TEFCA to connect participants and route queries between networks.
Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement: the federal framework that sets common rules for nationwide health information exchange.
A secure messaging standard for sending health information from one address to another, similar to encrypted email between providers.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: the HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web APIs.
Integrating the Healthcare Enterprise: a body that publishes profiles for how systems exchange data, such as document sharing and patient lookup.
Admit, discharge and transfer: the messages a hospital sends when a patient arrives, leaves or moves.
National Directory of Healthcare: the HL7 FHIR implementation guide that describes how providers, organizations and endpoints are listed in a directory.
The electronic address, usually a web URL or a Direct address, where an organization receives or serves health data.
